questions.explanation: Every command Parts 2-5 of the lab touch, in 23 rows. Knowing what a command is is the easy half; the rest of this quiz is the other half — which options change its behaviour, and which arguments tell it what to act on.

Long format: permissions, link count, owner, group, size and date
Reverses the sort order, so Z comes before A
Recurses into every subdirectory and lists their contents too
Used with -l, prints sizes in human-readable units (K, M, G)
Sorts by modification time, newest first
Sorts by file size, largest first
Appends a type marker to each name: / for a directory, * for an executable

questions.explanation: Combine them freely: ls -lah is the everyday listing — long format, hidden files included, sizes in K/M/G. The lab's ls -lr (Part 2, Step 2e) is the same idea with two flags.

questions.explanation: This is the options-vs-arguments distinction in one command. -l, -r and --help are options that change how ls behaves; labs, myfile.sh and Desktop are arguments that tell it what to act on. Part 2, Steps 2a-g.
